scope: Original deliberately faulty teaching fixtures. Weak suites assert exact outcomes but intentionally omit a distinguishing input. These are host Rust compiler/tests and independent Chialisp/Rue VM executions, not Rust-to-CLVM or consensus proofs.

studies.title: Coin ID used as a payment destination
studies.claim: Distinct SDK CoinId and PuzzleHash types reject this direct argument swap, even though both contain 32 bytes.
limitations: The guarantee relies on choosing distinct domain types. Deliberately wrapping coin_id.0 as PuzzleHash still compiles and needs policy review.
The equal-width Rue Bytes32 annotations do not express distinct domains. A separately executed Rue distinct-struct control rejects the same domain swap; this is not a unique Rust capability.

studies.title: Untested branch returns a condition instead of a condition list
studies.claim: The declared Rust return type requires both returning branches to produce a one-element condition tuple.
limitations: Consistent types do not establish correct condition opcodes or authorization. Both branches could return the same wrong well-typed policy.
The study evaluates CLVM return trees; it does not submit a coin spend to consensus.

studies.title: Approval code two is accidentally treated as true
studies.claim: Rust rejects an integer directly used as an if condition; it requires an explicit boolean expression.
limitations: Rust does not select the intended boolean expression. Writing approved != 0 would recreate the policy bug and compile.
The corrected fixture explicitly asserts approved == 1 at runtime; this policy is not proved by the type checker.
This host-only study does not claim project ABI or Rust-to-CLVM validation.

studies.title: A misspelled name survives an untested classic Chialisp branch
studies.claim: Rust resolves the amount name in both branches before tests execute; an undeclared amout cannot compile.
limitations: This behavior is measured with the classic chialisp 0.4.6 compiler path, not claimed for every Chialisp dialect or linter.
A typo that names another existing variable can still compile and requires stronger types or tests.

studies.title: Negative control: missing policy cap still compiles
studies.claim: A u64 return type does not prove the independently specified output limit of 1000.
limitations: Both the Chialisp and native Rust bugs compile. The missed witness needs a policy assertion, stronger tests or a separately stated model specification.
The existing bounded-counter SMT study verifies its explicit IR model; this experiment is not a compiler-preservation proof.
